Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1035
Claimant:
Jessica Walker
Adjuster:
Jerry Hanson
April 26, 2025
The claim was reported by phone the same day as the side impact at the intersection, and the claimant described the
crash as the other car entering on the passenger side. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer and said they
would handle the paperwork directly.
July 16, 2025
Police attended and confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle at the time, and the responding officer's notes match
the account given to us. The policyholder was not driving, but the driver lives in the same household and is covered
as a household member.
July 22, 2025
Photos taken at the scene confirm the point of impact and the general position of both vehicles, though no
independent witnesses have come forward. The damage to the claimant's vehicle appears mostly consistent with the
described impact.
August 23, 2025
The claimant reported a knee injury and attended urgent care the following day, where the findings were recorded in
line with the force of a side impact. No earlier injury to the same area is known from the claimant's records so far.
August 24, 2025
An inspection photo on file, taken before this crash, shows the same dent on the rear door, so the damage is not
entirely new. Nothing we have reviewed suggests the damage occurred before the coverage started.
October 20, 2025
The claimant has given the same account of the collision in each conversation, including the phone call, the recoredd
statement, and the follow-up call. Treatment has followed a usual course, with physiotherapy sessions tapering off as
the knee improved.
November 19, 2025
Based on the photos, police record, medical notes, and the consistent account, the claim is being assessed for
payment under the policy. The file will be sent to the handler for final review, with the inspection photo and the prior
dent noted for the record.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
